items.title: If the reasoning behind an influence move were fully visible, how confident would you be it serves the org?
items.description: Simple teaching model, not a measured curve: represents confidence that a given use of influence actually serves the org's good, as a function of how visible the real reasoning behind it would be if fully disclosed to everyone affected. Confidence tracks visibility closely at the extremes — reasoning that would look fine said aloud tends to be legitimate, reasoning that only works kept hidden tends not to be — which is exactly the mechanism L2's visibility test relies on.

params.name: visibilityPercent
params.label: How visible the real reasoning would be if fully disclosed

items.compute: const confidence = Math.round(5 + 90 * Math.pow(params.visibilityPercent / 100, 1.3)); return { confidence };

outputs.label: Confidence this move actually serves the org's good

items.title: As influence reaches organizational scale, how far does one bad-faith use of it reach?
items.description: Simple teaching model, not a measured curve: represents how many people are affected by a single bad-faith use of influence, as a function of how much organizational scale that influence has reached — from a junior engineer whose missteps mostly land on themselves, to a staff engineer whose framing reliably moves a launch decision. It's the same drift mechanism staying-principled describes, just multiplied by how many people the choice actually touches.

outputs.label: People affected by a single bad-faith use of that influence
